Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this game, where India triumphed over their arch-rivals Pakistan to secure their first win in the 2024 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup. This victory has lifted them off the bottom of the group, improving their net run rate from -2.9 to -1.217, while Pakistan remain in third place for now. But the excitement isn’t over yet on this Super Sunday. The 2016 champions, West Indies, are gearing up to face the tournament debutants, Scotland, right here in Dubai. Both teams are in search of their first points of the tournament, and that match is set to commence shortly. Our build-up has already begun for that game. Switch tabs and catch all the action. See you there. Cheers!

Smriti Mandhana is in for a chat, standing in for Harmanpreet Kaur. She says it's too soon to give an update on Harmanpreet's injury, but hopes she is fine. Adds that as a bowling unit, they followed the plans but could have done better with the bat. Talks about the net run rate and says they remained calculative considering that it was tough to time the ball. Concludes that they look forward to the next games and this win gives them momentum.

The captain of Pakistan Women, Fatima Sana Khan says they weren’t up to the mark with the bat. Admits they were around 10-15 runs short and she hopes they can bounce back in the next game. Ends by saying she enjoyed playing against India.

Arundhati Reddy is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for her 3 wickets. She says she has been bowling with the new ball and knew she would have to bowl a couple of overs upfront and it came good. Adds that it was hot but she is used to these kinds of conditions and she was focussing on keeping it simple and attacking the stumps with the variation in pace.
Time for the presentation ceremony...

Earlier, after opting to bat first, Pakistan struggled to find any rhythm in their innings. They failed to form meaningful partnerships, losing wickets at regular intervals. The inability to rotate strike compounded the pressure from dot balls, and when the batters attempted to break free with big shots, they ended up losing their wickets. At one stage, it seemed as though Pakistan would fall short of even reaching 100, but a valuable 28-run stand between Nida Dar and Syeda Aroob Shah ensured they managed to scrape together a total of 105. It was a collective bowling effort for India but Arundhati Reddy stood out with 3 wickets while Shreyanka Patil had two wickets to her name.

Many expected India to adopt an aggressive approach in the Powerplay, aiming to chase down the target quickly and improve their net run rate. However, they opted for a more cautious, safety-first approach. With only 105 on the board, Pakistan's bowlers were tasked with bailing the team out once again, just as they had done against Sri Lanka. Fatima Sana Khan and Co. gave a good account of themselves, not conceding even a single boundary in the Powerplay. India's cautious approach kept Pakistan in the game, and when Fatima struck twice in two balls, her side's belief grew stronger. However, Harmanpreet Kaur's composed presence at the crease helped calm the nerves in the Indian dressing room. With just 2 runs needed, Kaur hurt her neck while attempting to drag herself back into the crease and walked off. Sajana Sajeevan then came in and finished the game with 7 balls to spare.

India huff and puff their way to the first points of the World Cup! After the heavy defeat against New Zealand, Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. will be relieved to get on the board, though there will be questions asked about whether they could have pressed harder to improve their net run rate. Credit to Pakistan for dragging the game into the penultimate over. By doing so, they not only made India work for the win but also ensured that their net run rate didn't take a significant hit.

Commentary.Commentary: Another flighted delivery by Dar, low full toss, on middle and leg, Shafali Verma swings a bit too hard and loses her shape in the process. Swipes it straight to square leg. Shafali looking a little frustrated.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Nida Dar to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: More air given by Dar and this is on off, Shafali Verma steps out and makes it into a full toss. Times it well but it goes straight to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Nida Dar to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Offers flight does Dar, full and outside off, Smriti Mandhana walks across her stumps and slog sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for another single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Nida Dar to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dar serves it slower and shorter, wide on off, Smriti Mandhana cuts off the back foot but picks out the fielder at cover-point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Nida Dar to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slowed up by Dar, full and on off, Shafali Verma leans and drives it down to long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Nida Dar to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dar loops it up, full and outside off, Shafali Verma brings her bottom hand into play and drills it through covers. Beats the sliding cover fielder there to her left but the ball plugs in the outfield and Shafali will have to be content with two.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Nida Dar to Shafali Verma, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nida Dar comes into the attack now.
Mandhana finds mid off again! Sana keeps it full, around off, Smriti Mandhana uses her feet again and drives it with a straight bat but straight to Gull Feroza at mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Fatima Sana Khan to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitched up again by Sana, on off, Smriti Mandhana skips down the track and gets to the pitch of the ball. Drives it well but can't get it past mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Fatima Sana Khan to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Very full from Sana, on off, Smriti Mandhana takes it on the full and jams it out to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Fatima Sana Khan to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, around off, Shafali Verma lunges and knocks it down to long on for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! Pakistan cannot afford this! Sana sprays it beyond the tramline on off, Shafali Verma lets it go. The keeper, Muneeba Ali Siddiqi moves to her right but cannot cut it off. The ball gets past her and races away for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: A big appeal for LBW but that was heading down leg! Another in-drifter from Sana, full and on middle and leg, Shafali Verma plays across her front pad as she tries to flick it away. Gets beaten on the inside edge and gets hit on the front pad.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a good length, around off, Shafali Verma gets her weight on the front foot and times the drive to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: From over the wicket, full and slanting in on the pads, Smriti Mandhana nudges it off the pads to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flatter and shorter, on off, Smriti Mandhana cuts it towards cover-point where there is a slight misfield but the cover fielder does well to back it up and keeps it to a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up, full and on off, Smriti Mandhana presses forward and eases the drive to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sadia drops it short, on off, Smriti Mandhana rocks on the back foot quickly and slaps it past cover. The ball plugs a bit in the outfield. Two fielders give it a chase and cut it off. Another brace for Mandhana.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed across the batter, full in length, Smriti Mandhana goes for the drive away from her body and gets an outside edge that goes past short third. The ball does not have enough legs to reach the fence as the fielder mops it up. The umpire standing at the bowling end is asked to wait as the third umpire checks for a short run but both batters are fine on that count. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Good stop! Tossed up, full and on off, Smriti Mandhana lunges and drives it towards cover-point where Syeda Aroob Shah is quick to get to the right and dives to make the stop.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Sadia Iqbal to Smriti Mandhana, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sadia Iqbal will share the new ball from the other end!
Sana hurls it full and around off, Shafali Verma looks for the drive but gets an inside edge onto the pads and it rolls down the deck.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Given LBW but successfully overturned by Shafali Verma! Sana gets the ball to swing back into the right-hander. With the keeper up to the stumps, Shafali Verma is made to stay in her crease. She tries to work it away off her pads and gets beaten on the inside edge. Wears it on the front pad and up goes the finger. Shafali Verma reviews it immediately. Did she get some bat on it? Or does she think it is going down leg? The front-on replays show a clear gap between the bat and the pad. The Ball Tracking shows the ball to be doing a bit too much and going down leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling across the batter, on a good length, on off, Smriti Mandhana stays leg side of the ball and rides the bounce to punch it along the ground to deep cover for one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Fatima Sana Khan to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 108.5 kph, sliding onto the pads, on a fuller length, Shafali Verma plants her front foot across and clips it to deep backward square leg for one more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags the length back does Fatima but it is around the pads, Smriti Mandhana hangs back and flicks it to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Fatima Sana Khan to Smriti Mandhana, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Edged away! Fatima serves it full from over the wicket and around off, Shafali Verma takes a couple of steps down the track and tries to drive it down the ground. Gets an outside edge that rolls down to deep third for a run. Shafali and India are underway!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Fatima Sana Khan to Shafali Verma, 1 run.
